pull.title: KAFKA-21028: [2/2] Remove hamcrest from org.apache.kafka.streams.processor.internals package
pull.body:
Remove hamcrest from a subset of tests in the
`org.apache.kafka.streams.processor.internals` package by migrating to
JUnit assertions.

Reviewers: Ken Huang <s7133700@gmail.com>, Christo Lolov
 <lolovc@amazon.com>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body: Thanks for this! I have a couple of small comments and queries :)
Thanks for the patch, one minor comment

review_comments.body: You could do the same trick for expectedJoinKeyValues as you did for the other three, no?
Both here and elsewhere there are examples of seemingly extraneous wrappings into sets. Are they needed? If yes, shouldn't the underlying method return a set?
In a similar vein as my previous comment - is the HashSet wrapper needed, because if not then I believe you can just remove it rather than change the list to a set?
I think this message is redundant. We can remove it.

Thanks for the review! 

I initially kept the list to minimize changes because its duplicate keys prevent a direct replacement with `Map.of`. 

After looking through the history, it seems the test previously checked multiple records but now only compares the final map. I’ve updated it to use `Map.of`.

That’s an interesting question. From a quick look at the code, I think the set conversion is mainly to avoid asserting an order that `File.listFiles()` does not guarantee. These methods seem to simply collect directory entries for iteration, so returning a `List` also seems fine.

This also seems intended to check the assigned partitions without their order. 

After reading the code, I found they are sorted using `PARTITION_COMPARATOR`, so a small test enhancement to verify that order seems reasonable. I’ve sorted `expectedAssignment` and updated the assertion to compare the lists directly.
